item.research_question: How does the combination of mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering affect the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of an equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy, particularly regarding the formation of secondary phases due to interstitial elements?
item.material_system: Equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (Nb: 16.67 at%, Mo: 16.67 at%, Ta: 16.67 at%, W: 16.67 at%, V: 16.67 at%, Ti: 16.67 at%) with oxygen introduction
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying of elemental powders (≥99.9% purity) in a high energy planetary ball mill with stainless steel balls/vial at a ball-to-powder weight ratio of 13:1 under high purity argon for 40 h; followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) of the 40 h milled powders in a graphite die at 1400 °C for 10 min under 30 MPa pressure, with a heating rate of 100 °C/min and cooling to 500 °C at 300 °C/min
item.test_conditions: Room temperature compressive testing at a strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ on cylindrical samples (Φ3 mm × 6 mm); density measured by Archimedes' method; microstructure analyzed via XRD, SEM, TEM, and EDS
key_findings: The consolidated bulk HEA exhibits a compressive yield strength of 2709 MPa, fracture strength of 3115 MPa, and total fracture strain of 11.4%.
The sintered alloy consists of a BCC1 matrix phase, a minor BCC2 phase (3 vol%), and an FCC precipitated phase (16.1 vol%) identified as TiO.
The average grain size of the BCC1 matrix phase is 1.35 μm, significantly finer than the tens of microns observed in as-cast counterparts.
The average size of the FCC TiO precipitated particles is measured to be 0.64 μm.
The relative density of the bulk alloy is 96.75% with a measured density of 10.6 g/cm³.
The microhardness of the sintered alloy is 786 HV, which is higher than the 510 HV of the as-cast NbMoTaWVTi HEA.
The mass fraction of oxygen in the powders after 40 h of milling is measured to be 0.86%.
Compared to the as-cast HEA, the compressive yield strength is 78.8% higher and fracture strength is 45.9% higher.
item.mechanism: The excellent mechanical properties are attributed to a combination of solid solution strengthening from the atomic size difference of alloying elements, grain boundary strengthening due to the fine-grained BCC matrix (1.35 μm), and precipitation strengthening caused by the formation of TiO particles which impede dislocation motion.
item.limitations: The ductility of the sintered alloy decreases by about 20% compared to the as-cast HEA, and the fracture mechanism involves a combination of plastic and brittle fracture with intergranular fracture areas.
item.future_work: The authors state that mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering is a promising way to further improve mechanical properties of refractory HEAs by means of grain refinement and precipitation strengthening.
quotes: The compressive yield strength, fracture strength, and total fracture strain of the consolidated bulk HEA are 2709 MPa, 3115 MPa, and 11.4%, respectively.

The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles.
The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA.
